newsitem.title: UK: Battered gold set to regroup short term-chartists.
newsitem.headline: Battered gold set to regroup short term-chartists.

text.p: Gold's slide to the landmark $340 an ounce level on Friday should signal a consolidation period or even a brief rally before prices resume their inexorable decline, technical analysts said.

Bullion tumbled to fix at a near four-year low of $340.90 in the morning, after trading at 3-1/4 year lows in recent weeks. Prices then slid further to a low bid so far of $339.50 -- a decline of some $30 since the start of 1997.
But despite gold's overwhelmingly gloomy technical outlook, it may have seen its lows for the time being, several analysts said.

"Gold has reached important interim levels around $340 at a time when the market is creating divergence betwen the oscillators, such as the RSI (relative strength index), against the actual price level," said Cliff Green of Trend Analysis.
"The price is making new lows and the oscillator is moving higher, which highlights the vulnerablility for a correction in the next few days."
The 14-day RSI was at 25, versus a low of 14 in January.
Green said a sharp but shortlived corrective bounce could take prices to as high as $350 over the next couple of weeks.
But then gold would likely tumble towards the $325-$330 area, the lows for 1993.
Analysts at Elliot Wave International also saw prices rebounding in the short-term, having reached the important $341.60-$340.00 zone.
"The five wave decline from $357.30 suggests that this zone will produce at least a bounce toward the $346.75-$347.85 region before weakness resumes," analyst John Sowden said in a commentary.
A breach of the $340 area targetted $338-$337, he added.
Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge noted that $340 was significant psychologically as a round number as well as a notable support area from both 1993 and 1990.
"The good news is gold is oversold in the very long term. You have the 12-month RSI at 25, which is the most oversold it has been since at least 1985," she said.
"But there is no sign that the decline in slowing significantly. We may see some consolidation in this area, but I suspect it's going to feel a lot happier at $325."
The white metals are also likely to level off or possibly shoot higher in coming days, analysts said.
Silver, indicated at $4.79/$4.81, was near the bottom of a descending channel and looked like it could bounce off support at $4.77 and revisit the $4.87-$4.88 area, Green said.
"That could trigger a sharp bounce to the $5.05-$5.07 area, and then up to $5.20. Again, this will be short-lived," he said.
Platinum, like gold, achieved a key target when it reached $350 an ounce and charts exhibited a similar divergence between short-term RSI and prices. It was last at $349.00/$350.00.
"There is a possibility it will correct upwards or alternatively track sideways, negating the need for higher numbers before dribbling back down again," Green said.
